title: Hidden progress blindness
summary: The player expects obvious immediate gains and misses the slower improvements to consistency, confidence, and bad-run quality that aim training often produces.
telltales: The player quits or panics because progress no longer feels dramatic
Only ceiling moments are used to judge whether training works
contraindications: Do not use subtle-progress language to ignore a real bad routine or wrong scenario choice
avoid: Judging aim training only by whether today's in-game feel was obviously better
